title: The Matroid Secretary Conjecture is True
what was claimed: The matroid secretary conjecture and its strong e-competitive version are open.
what it proves: We resolve the matroid secretary conjecture, giving an online algorithm that accepts each element of the offline optimum with probability at least $1/4$. The algorithm only needs the number of elements in advance and independence-oracle access to subsets of already-arrived elements; it does not need to know the matroid upfront.

title: Settling the Matroid Secretary Problem
what was claimed: The matroid secretary conjecture and its strong e-competitive version are open.
what it proves: This paper settles the Matroid Secretary Problem with an $e$-probability-competitive algorithm. The algorithm is ordinal and accesses arrived elements only through comparison and independence oracles, and has expected polynomial time and oracle complexity.

title: Centered logarithmic Brunn?Minkowski inequality
what was claimed: The origin-symmetric logarithmic Brunn?Minkowski conjecture remains open in general dimension.
what it proves: The logarithmic Brunn--Minkowski and logarithmic Minkowski inequalities are proved for convex bodies whose centroids are at the origin, with equality precisely for independent positive dilations of common direct summands. This characterizes when centered convex bodies have the same cone-volume measure. The \(L_p\) Brunn--Minkowski and Minkowski inequalities are also obtained for every \(p>0\), with equality only for positive dilates, and the corresponding uniqueness of centered \(L_p\) surface area measures is established.

title: Existence of a non-sofic group
what was claimed: All countable groups may be sofic.
what it proves: OpenAI announced the existence of a non-sofic group: the unit group of the binary Leavitt algebra. We exhibit a different source of examples (relying on the same technical criterion) which includes torsion-free groups.

title: A central limit theorem for the random assignment problem
what was claimed: The central limit theorem for the random assignment cost is open.
what it proves: Proves sqrt(n)(C_n-zeta(2)) converges to a centered normal with variance 4*zeta(2)-4*zeta(3), for independent uniform costs. The proposed open CLT row must be excluded.

title: On the maximal dimension of an irreducible representation of the symmetric group
what was claimed: The existence of a sqrt(N)-order asymptotic constant for the largest Plancherel atom is open.
what it proves: Proves max_lambda dim(lambda)=sqrt(N!)*exp(-(d+o(1))*sqrt(N)) for some d>0, answering the Vershik-Kerov 1985 question. This closes the existence problem; it does not identify d explicitly.

title: Sharp asymptotics of disconnection time of large cylinders by simple and biased random walks
what was claimed: Sharp asymptotics for the simple-random-walk disconnection time of large discrete cylinders are open.
what it proves: Obtains the sharp lower bound matching Sznitman's 2009 upper bound for simple random walk on (Z/NZ)^d times Z, d>=2. The original sharp-asymptotics candidate is excluded.

title: Sub-optimality of Marton's Inner Bound for the Two-Receiver Broadcast Channel
what was claimed: Marton's inner bound may give the capacity region of every two-receiver broadcast channel.
what it proves: Reports strict suboptimality of Marton's inner bound. This rules out identifying that inner bound with the unrestricted general capacity region.

title: Almost all graphs are determined by their generalized spectrum
what was claimed: Almost all graphs may still be unknown to be determined by their generalized spectrum.
what it proves: Proves the generalized-spectrum version of Haemers's conjecture. The ordinary adjacency-spectrum version remains explicitly open and is a separate target.

title: Anticoncentration of the Permanent in Ginibre Ensembles
what was claimed: The permanent anti-concentration conjecture for a complex Gaussian matrix remains open.
what it proves: Claims the permanent anti-concentration conjecture, with small-ball estimates for Gaussian matrix permanents; exclude this candidate pending independent review of the claimed proof.

title: Tight lower bounds for anti-concentration of Rademacher sums and Tomaszewski's counterpart problem
what was claimed: The Hitczenko-Kwapien lower bound 7/32 for a normalized Rademacher sum is open.
what it proves: Resolves the conjectured 7/32 bound and determines the optimal lower-tail function. Restricted-case papers after this announcement must not be mistaken for the current status.

title: Symmetrization for finitely dependent colouring
what was claimed: Existence of an isometry-invariant finitely dependent 4-coloring of Z^d is open.
what it proves: Constructs an isometry-invariant finitely dependent proper 4-coloring of Z^d, with a finitary IID coding having exponentially decaying coding-radius tails.

title: A proof of the strong Gaussian product inequality conjecture
what was claimed: The Gaussian product inequality for arbitrary positive exponents remains an open problem.
what it proves: Claims E product_i |X_i|^alpha_i >= product_i E |X_i|^alpha_i for every centered Gaussian vector and all alpha_i>0, with equality characterized by independence when marginal variances are positive. This candidate is excluded from the open rows.

title: Long time derivation of the Boltzmann equation from hard sphere dynamics
what was claimed: Derivation from hard spheres is restricted to the short time of Lanford's theorem.
what it proves: Derives the Boltzmann equation for arbitrarily long fixed times on which its classical solution exists. The opened January 2026 Bourbaki account 2602.04407 independently explains this same scope. Do not relist extension beyond Lanford time as open; this does not prove global classical Boltzmann existence for large data.

title: A regularized Kellerer theorem in arbitrary dimension
what was claimed: Every multidimensional peacock might admit a mimicking Markov martingale without further hypotheses.
what it proves: The inspected latest abstract states counterexamples in d>=2 showing that regularization is necessary to guarantee a mimicking Markov martingale; it proves a strong Markov Ito-diffusion construction after Gaussian regularization. The unrestricted multidimensional candidate is not written as open.

title: Scope check on the claimed integrated-fractional-Brownian persistence refutation
what was claimed: The abstract of 2509.10265v11 says the equality theta_(2,H)=H(1-H) has been refuted.
what it proves: PDF p.5, viewed in papers/molchan_page5.png: Statement 1.2 gives monotonicity; Consequences 1 invokes the natural assumption of strict decrease to rule out the symmetric formula. Thus the displayed refutation argument has an additional assumption at precisely that step. In any event the paper does not calculate the general finite-order exponent sought in T226. Record this scope difference rather than treating its abstract as an exact-exponent solution.

title: High-dimensional hot-spots caveat on T030 is false
what was claimed: The live caveat says the hot-spots problem remains open in higher dimensions.
what it proves: Convex bounded counterexamples for all sufficiently large dimensions. Does not settle the planar row. This is a pre-August scope correction discovered during the audit.

title: Fixed-degree random-regular-graph bulk universality component of T054 is solved
what was claimed: Bulk universality together with an unspecified QUE remainder is retained as a live problem.

paper.locator: PDF p.3, Theorem 1.1 (Gap and fixed-energy correlation universality)

what it proves: Gap and fixed-energy correlation universality for every fixed d>=3. This is a solved component, not a claim that an unspecified strong QUE assertion is proved.

title: Very-dense random-graph chromatic CLT in interior clique windows
what was claimed: The Surya-Warnke Gaussian-fluctuation prediction in very dense random graphs.
what it proves: Chromatic CLT for G(n,1-p) in stated interior clique windows n^(-2/r)(log n)^(1/binom(r,2)) << p << n^(-2/(r+1)), r>=2. Does not settle fixed p=1/2 concentration T058 or endpoints.

title: Kahn-Saks large-width balancing conjecture
what was claimed: Sufficiently large poset width forces a nearly balanced pair in a uniform random linear extension.
what it proves: For every desired closeness to 1/2, sufficiently large width forces balance that close to 1/2 (Theorem 1 as described in the primary abstract). Does not prove the 1/3-2/3 conjecture for all bounded-width posets T112.

title: Finiteness of two-dimensional stationary sandpile avalanches
what was claimed: Every avalanche from adding one grain to the infinite-volume stationary sandpile on Z^2 is finite almost surely.
what it proves: Almost-sure finiteness, with the radius tail bounded by a negative power of log R. Does not identify the power-law avalanche exponents asked in T100.

title: Sapozhnikov-Shiraishi characterization conjecture, three-dimensional case
what was claimed: A characterization of the 3D loop-erased-random-walk scaling limit by the continuous recovery property.
what it proves: The abstract explicitly resolves the 3D case, uniquely characterizes the LERW/RWLC scaling limits and derives inversion invariance. It does not identify the exact LERW growth exponent asked in T103.

title: Oriented Kesten-McKay law for fixed-degree uniform random regular digraphs
what was claimed: T141 retains the fixed-degree global empirical eigenvalue law as open.
what it proves: The live row asks for fixed d>=3, the uniform simple loopless directed d-regular graph and weak convergence in probability to density d^2(d-1)/(pi(d^2-|z|^2)^2) on |z|<sqrt(d). The theorem proves the identical statement for every fixed d>=2.

title: Irreducibility of random 0–1 polynomials (Odlyzko–Poonen)
what was claimed: The 0-1 irreducibility conjecture was proved only under GRH and remained open unconditionally.

paper.title: The Odlyzko-Poonen Conjecture on Irreducibility of Random Polynomials

what it proves: Theorem 1.1, PDF page 1, proves the exact constant-term-one Odlyzko-Poonen conjecture unconditionally.

title: Recurrence of the planar Eulerian walker with iid uniform rotors and clockwise mechanism
what was claimed: The live T178 status said no result was known on Z^d with d>=2.
what it proves: Theorem 1.1(i), PDF page 2, proves almost-sure recurrence on the square lattice with the clockwise mechanism and independent uniform initial rotors. The higher-dimensional part of T178 remains outside this theorem.
limitation: Only the stated planar mechanism is matched; full proof not independently audited.
